inputs.original_text: Phoenix leaders voted Wednesday night to tighten restrictions on ICE and other law enforcement agencies using city property. That’s a necessary step toward making public spaces accountable to the people who live in them, rather than automatically available to federal enforcement. Calling this a threat to safety ignores how aggressive enforcement can put immigrant communities and other vulnerable residents at risk. Community safety means protecting people’s rights and trust, not treating cooperation with law enforcement as an end in itself.
inputs.modified_text: Phoenix leaders voted Wednesday night to tighten restrictions on ICE and other law enforcement agencies using city property. That matters because public spaces should serve the people who live in them, not automatically become tools of enforcement. Immigrant communities and other vulnerable residents bear the cost when aggressive policing erodes trust and makes public spaces feel unsafe. Real community safety means protecting people’s rights and dignity—not treating cooperation with law enforcement as the only measure of success.
